@graph.name: Intradermal capsaicin produces widespread oscillatory cortical activation absent from paired vehicle trials
@graph.description: Does capsaicin-induced acute pain produce cortical autofluorescence activity that the microscope can detect against a paired vehicle control?
@graph.nrr:successCriteria: Cortical activation after capsaicin injection that is clearly absent after the paired vehicle injection in the same mouse.

nrr:applicabilityConditions.anesthesia: 3-4% isoflurane for induction; maintained at 1.25-1.5% during imaging (from trial file names); depth confirmed by loss of righting reflex, ~1 breath per second, no toe-pinch response
nrr:applicabilityConditions.preparation: head-fixed with earbars in a stereotaxic frame (Kopf); heating pad; hair removed with Nair; eye ointment; 1 mL body-temperature sterile saline subcutaneous; 0.1 mL 1% lidocaine subcutaneous under the scalp; scalp removed; periosteum cleaned; thin layer of cyanoacrylate glue applied to the skull for optical clarity
nrr:applicabilityConditions.invasiveness: through-skull, label-free; no craniotomy, no transgenic animals, no dye or virus injection
nrr:applicabilityConditions.readout: flavoprotein autofluorescence, dF/F over a region of interest
nrr:applicabilityConditions.imaging: 10 frames per second, 13.4 x 11.3 mm, 5 um/px with no binning; cropped to the brain and binned 4 x 4 for all trials
nrr:applicabilityConditions.analysis: temporal averaging: 2 frames for tactile trials, 8 frames for injection trials, to reduce noise; motion correction by SIFT-based registration; brain masking by flood fill (scikit-image flood); bleach correction: subtract the bottom 5% of pixels within the brain from each frame; baseline autofluorescence subtraction
nrr:applicabilityConditions.statistics: none reported; no significance testing, no power analysis, no detection limit stated anywhere in the pub

nrr:cost.note: 13 imaging trials across 5 mice. The pub reports the imaging system cost (approximately US$30,000 including the camera) as capital, not as the cost of this study; no per-study cost is given.
nrr:cost.source: Methods, Microscope and sensory stimulation hardware

nrr:provenanceNotes: Order confound flagged by the authors: oscillatory activity was more intense for a hindlimb previously injected with vehicle than for a hindlimb that only received capsaicin, so injection order may contribute
Effect values are the authors' qualitative descriptions; no numeric dF/F is tabulated for injection trials.

nrr:aiUseDeclaration.statement: We used ChatGPT to help write and clean up code, and GitHub Copilot to help write and add comments to our code.

nrr:confidence.basis: consistent across three injection sites with paired vehicle controls, but n = 1 per condition, no statistics, and an order effect the authors flag

@graph.nrr:outcomeSummary: widespread, high-intensity cortical activation for ~10 minutes after injection, absent in vehicle trials; complex and oscillatory; nape injection produced briefer activity confined to the somatosensory area of one hemisphere

complianceIds: All animal work performed in accordance with the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee of the Charles River Accelerator and Development Lab (CRADL, South San Francisco, CA). No protocol number is given in the pub.
